passages.text: After the king had settled into his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all his enemies around him, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Here I am, living in a house of cedar, while the ark of God remains in a tent.”
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
God gave David rest from all his enemies.
David lived in his own house.
His house was made of cedar wood.
David spoke to Nathan.
Nathan was a prophet.
David said, “Look at me.
I live in a house of cedar.
But the ark of God stays in a tent.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י כִּי־ יָשַׁ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּבֵית֑וֹ וַיהוָ֛ה הֵנִֽיחַ־ ל֥וֹ מִסָּבִ֖יב מִכָּל־ אֹיְבָֽיו׃ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ אֶל־ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא רְאֵ֣ה נָ֔א אָנֹכִ֥י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּבֵ֣ית אֲרָזִ֑ים וַֽאֲרוֹן֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים יֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּת֥וֹךְ הַיְרִיעָֽה׃

passages.text: And Nathan replied to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the LORD is with you.”
passages.sermon:
Nathan was a prophet.
The king was David.
Nathan spoke to King David.
Nathan said, “Do everything in your heart.
Go and do it.
The LORD is with you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר נָתָן֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּֽלְבָבְךָ֖ לֵ֣ךְ עֲשֵׂ֑ה כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: But that night the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying, “Go and tell My servant David that this is what the LORD says: Are you the one to build for Me a house to dwell in?
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Nathan that night.
The LORD gave Nathan a message.
The LORD told Nathan to speak to David.
David was the servant of the LORD.
The LORD said, “This is what I say.”
The LORD asked David, “Are you the one to build a house for Me to live in?”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ נָתָ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃ לֵ֤ךְ וְאָֽמַרְתָּ֙ אֶל־ עַבְדִּ֣י אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה הַאַתָּ֛ה תִּבְנֶה־ לִּ֥י בַ֖יִת לְשִׁבְתִּֽי׃

passages.text: For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought the Israelites up out of Egypt until this day, but I have moved about with a tent as My dwelling.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Nathan the prophet.
God told Nathan to speak to David, the king of Israel.
God said, “I did not live in a house.
I brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
From that day until today, I have not lived in a house.
I moved with My people.
I lived in a tent.
I lived in a tabernacle.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָשַׁ֙בְתִּי֙ בְּבַ֔יִת לְ֠מִיּוֹם הַעֲלֹתִ֞י אֶת־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְעַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וָאֶֽהְיֶה֙ מִתְהַלֵּ֔ךְ בְּאֹ֖הֶל וּבְמִשְׁכָּֽן׃

passages.text: In all My journeys with all the Israelites, have I ever asked any of the leaders I appointed to shepherd My people Israel, ‘Why haven’t you built Me a house of cedar?’
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Nathan at night.
God told Nathan to speak to David.
God reminded Nathan about His actions with Israel.
God said He traveled with all the Israelites.
God said He never stayed in one place.
God appointed leaders over Israel.
God commanded these leaders to care for His people.
God never asked any leader this question.
God never said, “Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?”
passages.original: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־ הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־ אַחַד֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתִי לִרְע֛וֹת אֶת־ עַמִּ֥י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹֽא־ בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃

passages.text: Now then, you are to tell My servant David that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: I took you from the pasture, from following the flock, to be the ruler over My people Israel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is speaking.
The LORD commands a message for David.
David is the LORD’s servant.
The LORD says, “I took you, David, from the pasture.”
David was following the flock.
The LORD took David from behind the sheep.
The LORD made David ruler over His people.
The LORD’s people are Israel.
passages.original: וְ֠עַתָּה כֹּֽה־ תֹאמַ֞ר לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְדָוִ֗ד כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֲנִ֤י לְקַחְתִּ֙יךָ֙ מִן־ הַנָּוֶ֔ה מֵאַחַ֖ר הַצֹּ֑אן לִֽהְי֣וֹת נָגִ֔יד עַל־ עַמִּ֖י עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have cut off all your enemies from before you. Now I will make for you a name like the greatest in the land.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to David.
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God said, “I have been with you everywhere you have gone.
I removed all your enemies from before you.
I will make your name great.
Your name will be like the names of the greatest people on earth.”
passages.original: וָאֶהְיֶ֣ה עִמְּךָ֗ בְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלַ֔כְתָּ וָאַכְרִ֥תָה אֶת־ כָּל־ אֹיְבֶ֖יךָ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ וְעָשִׂ֤תִֽי לְךָ֙ שֵׁ֣ם גָּד֔וֹל כְּשֵׁ֥ם הַגְּדֹלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: And I will provide a place for My people Israel and will plant them so that they may dwell in a place of their own and be disturbed no more. No longer will the sons of wickedness oppress them as they did at the beginning and have done since the day I appointed judges over My people Israel. I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD declares to you that He Himself will establish a house for you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to David.
The LORD will give His people Israel a place.
The LORD will plant Israel in this place.
Israel will live there.
Israel will not be disturbed again.
Evil people will not oppress Israel anymore.
Evil people oppressed Israel in the beginning.
Evil people oppressed Israel since the LORD appointed judges over Israel.
The LORD will give David rest from all his enemies.
The LORD Himself will make a house for David.
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י מָ֠קוֹם לְעַמִּ֨י לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל וּנְטַעְתִּיו֙ וְשָׁכַ֣ן תַּחְתָּ֔יו וְלֹ֥א יִרְגַּ֖ז ע֑וֹד וְלֹֽא־ יֹסִ֤יפוּ בְנֵֽי־ עַוְלָה֙ לְעַנּוֹת֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בָּרִאשׁוֹנָֽה׃ וּלְמִן־ הַיּ֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוִּ֤יתִי שֹֽׁפְטִים֙ עַל־ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַהֲנִיחֹ֥תִי לְךָ֖ מִכָּל־ אֹיְבֶ֑יךָ וְהִגִּ֤יד לְךָ֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּי־ בַ֖יִת יַעֲשֶׂה־ לְּךָ֥ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And when your days are fulfilled and you rest with your fathers, I will raise up your descendant after you, who will come from your own body, and I will establish his kingdom.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to King David.
God promised David a future.
God said, “When your days are complete, you will die and rest with your ancestors.”
God said, “After you die, I will raise up your descendant.”
This descendant will come from your own body.
I will establish his kingdom.
passages.original: כִּ֣י׀ יִמְלְא֣וּ יָמֶ֗יךָ וְשָֽׁכַבְתָּ֙ אֶת־ אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲקִימֹתִ֤י אֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֙ אַחֲרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֵצֵ֖א מִמֵּעֶ֑יךָ וַהֲכִינֹתִ֖י אֶת־ מַמְלַכְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He will build a house for My Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to David about his descendant.
This descendant will build a house for God’s Name.
God will establish the throne of this descendant’s kingdom.
God will make this throne last forever.
passages.original: ה֥וּא יִבְנֶה־ בַּ֖יִת לִשְׁמִ֑י וְכֹנַנְתִּ֛י אֶת־ כִּסֵּ֥א מַמְלַכְתּ֖וֹ עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: I will be his Father, and he will be My son. When he does wrong, I will discipline him with the rod of men and with the blows of the sons of men.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to David about his descendant.
God said, “I will be a Father to him.
He will be a son to Me.
If he does wrong, I will correct him.
I will use human punishment to discipline him.
I will use the blows that men give to discipline him.”
passages.original: אֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶה־ לּ֣וֹ לְאָ֔ב וְה֖וּא יִהְיֶה־ לִּ֣י לְבֵ֑ן אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּהַ֣עֲוֺת֔וֹ וְהֹֽכַחְתִּיו֙ בְּשֵׁ֣בֶט אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וּבְנִגְעֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃

passages.text: But My loving devotion will never be removed from him as I removed it from Saul, whom I moved out of your way.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to David about his descendant.
God promised His loving devotion.
God said, “I will never remove My loving devotion from him.”
God removed His loving devotion from Saul.
God took Saul away from before David.
God will not do this to David’s descendant.
passages.original: וְחַסְדִּ֖י לֹא־ יָס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר הֲסִרֹ֙תִי֙ מֵעִ֣ם שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲסִרֹ֖תִי מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Your house and kingdom will endure forever before Me, and your throne will be established forever.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to David.
God made a promise to David.
God said David’s house will last forever.
God said David’s kingdom will last forever.
God said David’s throne will stand firm forever.
God said all this will be before Him.
passages.original: וְנֶאְמַ֨ן בֵּיתְךָ֧ וּמַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ עַד־ עוֹלָ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כִּֽסְאֲךָ֔ יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן עַד־ עוֹלָֽם׃

passages.text: So Nathan relayed to David all the words of this entire vision.
passages.sermon:
Nathan was a prophet.
Nathan received a vision from God.
The vision contained many words.
Nathan spoke all these words to David.
Nathan told David everything from the vision.
passages.original: כְּכֹל֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וּכְכֹ֖ל הַחִזָּי֣וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה כֵּ֛ן דִּבֶּ֥ר נָתָ֖ן אֶל־ דָּוִֽד׃ס

passages.text: Then King David went in, sat before the LORD, and said, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that You have brought me this far?
passages.sermon:
King David was the ruler of Israel.
David went in and sat before the LORD.
David spoke to God.
David said, "Who am I, O Lord GOD?"
David said, "Who is my family?"
David said, "You have brought me this far."
David recognized that God had raised him and his family to this place.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מִ֣י אָנֹכִ֞י אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ וּמִ֣י בֵיתִ֔י כִּ֥י הֲבִיאֹתַ֖נִי עַד־ הֲלֹֽם׃

passages.text: And as if this was a small thing in Your eyes, O Lord GOD, You have also spoken about the future of the house of Your servant. Is this Your custom with man, O Lord GOD?
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD showed great kindness to David.
The Lord GOD did not see His blessings as a small thing.
The Lord GOD spoke about the future of David’s house.
The Lord GOD promised good things for David’s descendants.
David asked if this is how the Lord GOD treats people.
David wondered if this is the way the Lord GOD acts with mankind.
passages.original: וַתִּקְטַן֩ ע֨וֹד זֹ֤את בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֛ר גַּ֥ם אֶל־ בֵּֽית־ עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְמֵֽרָח֑וֹק וְזֹ֛את תּוֹרַ֥ת הָאָדָ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

passages.text: What more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, O Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
David was the king of Israel.
David spoke to the Lord God.
David said, “What more can I say to You?”
You, Lord God, know Your servant.
You know everything about me.
passages.original: וּמַה־ יּוֹסִ֥יף דָּוִ֛ד ע֖וֹד לְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֑יךָ וְאַתָּ֛ה יָדַ֥עְתָּ אֶֽת־ עַבְדְּךָ֖ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

passages.text: For the sake of Your word and according to Your own heart, You have accomplished this great thing and revealed it to Your servant.
passages.sermon:
God acted for the sake of His word.
God acted according to His own heart.
God accomplished this great thing.
God revealed this great thing to His servant.
passages.original: בַּעֲב֤וּר דְּבָֽרְךָ֙ וּֽכְלִבְּךָ֔ עָשִׂ֕יתָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַגְּדוּלָּ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את לְהוֹדִ֖יעַ אֶת־ עַבְדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: How great You are, O Lord GOD! For there is none like You, and there is no God but You, according to everything we have heard with our own ears.
passages.sermon:
David speaks to God.
David calls God "O Lord GOD."
God is great.
No one is like God.
No other god exists except God.
Everything we have heard confirms this.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֥ן גָּדַ֖לְתָּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כִּֽי־ אֵ֣ין כָּמ֗וֹךָ וְאֵ֤ין אֱלֹהִים֙ זֽוּלָתֶ֔ךָ בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ בְּאָזְנֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: And who is like Your people Israel—the one nation on earth whom God went out to redeem as a people for Himself and to make a name for Himself? You performed great and awesome wonders by driving out nations and their gods from before Your people, whom You redeemed for Yourself from Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God chose the people of Israel.
Israel is the only nation on earth that God redeemed for Himself.
God made Israel His own people.
God gave Himself a name through Israel.
God did great and awesome wonders for Israel.
God drove out other nations and their gods from before Israel.
God redeemed Israel for Himself from Egypt.
passages.original: וּמִ֤י כְעַמְּךָ֙ כְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גּ֥וֹי אֶחָ֖ד בָּאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָלְכֽוּ־ אֱ֠לֹהִים לִפְדּֽוֹת־ ל֨וֹ לְעָ֜ם וְלָשׂ֧וּם ל֣וֹ שֵׁ֗ם וְלַעֲשׂ֨וֹת לָכֶ֜ם הַגְּדוּלָּ֤ה וְנֹֽרָאוֹת֙ לְאַרְצֶ֔ךָ מִפְּנֵ֣י עַמְּךָ֗ אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּדִ֤יתָ לְּךָ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם גּוֹיִ֖ם וֵאלֹהָֽיו׃

passages.text: For You have established Your people Israel as Your very own forever, and You, O LORD, have become their God.
passages.sermon:
God chose the people of Israel.
God made Israel His own people.
God did this forever.
The LORD became the God of Israel.
passages.original: וַתְּכ֣וֹנֵֽן לְ֠ךָ אֶת־ עַמְּךָ֨ יִשְׂרָאֵ֧ל׀ לְךָ֛ לְעָ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם וְאַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה הָיִ֥יתָ לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃ס

passages.text: And now, O LORD God, confirm forever the word You have spoken concerning Your servant and his house. Do as You have promised, so that Your name will be magnified forever when it is said, ‘The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel.’ And the house of Your servant David will be established before You.
passages.sermon:
The LORD God spoke a word about His servant David and David’s house.
God made a promise about David and his descendants.
Now, God, confirm this word forever.
Do what You have promised.
Let Your name become great forever.
Let people say, “The LORD of Hosts is God over Israel.”
Let the house of Your servant David stand firm before You.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהִ֔ים הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבַּ֤רְתָּ עַֽל־ עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְעַל־ בֵּית֔וֹ הָקֵ֖ם עַד־ עוֹלָ֑ם וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּֽרְתָּ׃ וְיִגְדַּ֨ל שִׁמְךָ֤ עַד־ עוֹלָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֱלֹהִ֖ים עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּבֵית֙ עַבְדְּךָ֣ דָוִ֔ד יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן לְפָנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: For You, O LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, have revealed this to Your servant when You said, ‘I will build a house for you.’ Therefore Your servant has found the courage to offer this prayer to You.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
You, LORD, revealed something to Your servant.
You said, "I will build a house for you."
Because of this, Your servant found courage.
Your servant prayed this prayer to You.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אַתָּה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל גָּלִ֜יתָה אֶת־ אֹ֤זֶן עַבְדְּךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בַּ֖יִת אֶבְנֶה־ לָּ֑ךְ עַל־ כֵּ֗ן מָצָ֤א עַבְדְּךָ֙ אֶת־ לִבּ֔וֹ לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלֶ֔יךָ אֶת־ הַתְּפִלָּ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: And now, O Lord GOD, You are God! Your words are true, and You have promised this goodness to Your servant.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD is the one true God.
He is the God of Israel.
He speaks words that are always true.
He promised good things to His servant David.
God told David about this goodness.
God’s promises are trustworthy.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אַתָּה־ הוּא֙ הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּדְבָרֶ֖יךָ יִהְי֣וּ אֱמֶ֑ת וַתְּדַבֵּר֙ אֶֽל־ עַבְדְּךָ֔ אֶת־ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: Now therefore, may it please You to bless the house of Your servant, that it may continue forever before You. For You, O Lord GOD, have spoken, and with Your blessing the house of Your servant will be blessed forever.”
passages.sermon:
David is speaking to the Lord God.
David calls himself God's servant.
David asks God to bless his house.
David wants his house to last forever before God.
David says that God has spoken this promise.
David says that God's blessing will make his house blessed forever.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הוֹאֵל֙ וּבָרֵךְ֙ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית עַבְדְּךָ֔ לִהְי֥וֹת לְעוֹלָ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כִּֽי־ אַתָּ֞ה אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ דִּבַּ֔רְתָּ וּמִבִּרְכָ֣תְךָ֔ יְבֹרַ֥ךְ בֵּֽית־ עַבְדְּךָ֖ לְעוֹלָֽם׃פ
